name: Visitor Visa / Visa-Exempt Entry
description: Taiwan offers visa-exempt entry and visitor visas for short-term stays covering tourism, business visits, and other non-employment activities. The published duration varies from 14 to 90 days depending on nationality and entry type.
tagline: Short-term entry for tourism, business visits, and transit
keyRequirement: Valid passport from a visa-exempt country (30-90 days) or visitor visa from TECO
targetAudience: Business visitors attending meetings, conferences, or trade fairs
Individuals exploring Taiwan before committing to a longer stay

eligibility.label: Valid passport with at least 6 months remaining validity
eligibility.description: Published requirements specify that the passport must be valid for at least 6 months from the date of entry.

eligibility.label: Visa-exempt nationality or visitor visa from TECO
eligibility.description: Nationals of visa-exempt countries may enter without a visa for the published duration (30-90 days depending on nationality). Others must obtain a visitor visa from a TECO office before travel.

eligibility.label: Return or onward ticket
eligibility.description: A confirmed return or onward ticket may be required at the point of entry. Published requirements vary by nationality.

eligibility.label: Proof of sufficient funds
eligibility.description: Immigration officers may request proof of financial means to support the intended stay. There is no single published minimum, but community members report that having the equivalent of TWD 20,000-30,000 is generally sufficient.

eligibilityQuestions.question: Is your passport valid for at least 6 months from your planned entry date?
eligibilityQuestions.helpText: Published requirements specify at least 6 months of passport validity.
eligibilityQuestions.disqualifyingMessage: Published entry requirements include a passport valid for at least 6 months.

eligibilityQuestions.question: Is your nationality on the published list of visa-exempt countries for Taiwan?
eligibilityQuestions.helpText: Check the Bureau of Consular Affairs (BOCA) website for the current visa-exempt country list.
eligibilityQuestions.disqualifyingMessage: Nationals not on the visa-exempt list must obtain a visitor visa from a TECO office before travel.

duration.initial: 30-90 days depending on nationality (visa-exempt) or as specified on visitor visa
duration.extension: Extensions may be possible at NIA for up to 180 days total in some cases
duration.maxTotal: Varies by nationality and visa type. Published maximum for visa-exempt stays is typically 90 days.

fees.application: Visa-exempt: free. Visitor visa: varies by nationality and TECO office (typically USD 50-160)
fees.notes: Visa-exempt entry has no fee. Visitor visa fees are published by each TECO office.

documents.name: Valid Passport
documents.description: Valid for at least 6 months from date of entry, with at least one blank page for entry stamps

documents.name: Return or Onward Ticket
documents.description: Confirmed booking showing departure from Taiwan within the allowed stay period
tips: Immigration officers may check for this at the port of entry

documents.name: Proof of Accommodation
documents.description: Hotel reservation or letter of invitation from a host in Taiwan

documents.name: Proof of Sufficient Funds
documents.description: Bank statement, credit card, or cash equivalent to support the intended stay

documents.name: Visitor Visa Application (if not visa-exempt)
documents.description: Completed visa application form submitted to a TECO office

applicationSteps.title: Check Visa-Exempt Status
applicationSteps.description: Verify whether your nationality is on the published visa-exempt list for Taiwan. The list is maintained by the Bureau of Consular Affairs (BOCA).

applicationSteps.title: Apply for Visitor Visa (if required)
applicationSteps.description: If not visa-exempt, apply at the TECO office with jurisdiction over your location. Submit the application form, passport, photo, and any required supporting documents.

applicationSteps.title: Enter Taiwan
applicationSteps.description: Present your passport (and visa if applicable) at immigration. The immigration officer determines the length of stay granted upon entry.
tips: Have your return ticket and accommodation proof readily available
Entry decisions are at the discretion of the immigration officer at the port of entry

applicationSteps.title: Register if Staying Over 90 Days
applicationSteps.description: If granted a stay exceeding 90 days (e.g., through a visitor visa extension), registration with NIA may be required.

processingTime.typical: Visa-exempt: immediate upon arrival. Visitor visa: 3-7 business days at TECO.
processingTime.notes: Visa-exempt entry requires no advance processing. Visitor visa processing times vary by TECO office.

restrictions: No work of any kind is permitted on a visitor visa or visa-exempt entry
Remote work for a foreign employer is a gray area — the Digital Nomad Visa is designed for that purpose
Business activities are limited to meetings, conferences, and non-employment activities
workPermission.notes: Working in Taiwan without a valid work permit is prohibited under published regulations. Violations may result in fines, deportation, and entry bans.

faqs.question: How long can visa-exempt visitors stay in Taiwan?
faqs.answer: Published durations vary by nationality: most Western countries receive 90 days visa-exempt, some countries receive 30 or 14 days. Check the BOCA visa-exempt list for the specific duration for your nationality.

faqs.question: Can the visa-exempt stay be extended?
faqs.answer: Published rules generally allow extensions in limited circumstances. An extension application may be submitted at a local NIA service center before the current stay expires. Extensions are not guaranteed and are at the discretion of NIA.

faqs.question: What is a 'visa run' and is it advisable?
faqs.answer: A visa run involves leaving Taiwan and re-entering to obtain a new entry period. While not prohibited, published regulations do not guarantee re-entry. Immigration officers have discretion and may deny entry to individuals with patterns of repeated short exits and re-entries.

faqs.question: Does time on a visitor visa count toward APRC?
faqs.answer: No. Published APRC requirements specify that only time spent on qualifying residence permits (such as ARC or Gold Card) counts toward the continuous residency requirement.

faqs.question: Can a visitor visa be converted to a work visa in Taiwan?
faqs.answer: Generally, a change of status from visitor to a work-based residence permit requires departing Taiwan and applying for the appropriate visa at a TECO office abroad. Some exceptions may apply — verify with NIA for the specific situation.

tips: Check the published visa-exempt duration for your specific nationality on the BOCA website before travel
Have a return ticket and proof of accommodation ready — immigration officers may request these at the port of entry
Carry sufficient funds or a bank statement, as proof of financial means may be requested
Overstaying the permitted duration results in fines and potential entry bans under published regulations
If planning to work in Taiwan, apply for the appropriate work visa (Gold Card, Work ARC, or DNV) instead
warnings: No work is permitted on a visitor visa or visa-exempt entry
Overstaying carries published penalties including fines and entry bans
Re-entry is not guaranteed — immigration officers have discretion at the border
Time on a visitor visa does NOT count toward APRC residency

communityTips.tip: Community members report that having a return ticket ready is the most commonly checked item at immigration
Frequent visa runs may attract additional scrutiny from immigration officers according to community reports
